sources.entry: TREK - Collaborative trip planner with interactive maps, day-by-day itineraries, budgets, packing lists, reservations, journey journaling, and PWA support. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: TREK is a self-hosted, real-time collaborative travel planner covering itineraries, maps, bookings, costs, packing, journaling and an optional AI assistant.
summary.what_it_does: TREK organizes a trip into day plans where places, notes and bookings can be dragged between days, with maps in Leaflet, Mapbox GL or MapLibre GL. It includes route sorting and travel modes over OSRM or Valhalla, public transport itineraries, GPX/KML/KMZ import and export, and a 16-day weather forecast. Bookings cover 18 reservation types, flight and train legs, file attachments, and import of confirmations via KItinerary or an AI model. A cost module splits expenses in cents with settle-up suggestions and CSV export, and packing lists and to-dos are included. Members collaborate in real time over WebSocket, with permissions, invite links, a read-only public share page, and group chat. Optional addons add a journal, tours (hiking, cycling, paddling, skiing), a photo book studio, a leave calendar, an atlas of visited countries, plugins, and an AI assistant with MCP server.
use_cases: plan a multi-day trip with friends
organize flight and hotel confirmations in one place
build a packing list for a trip
keep a travel journal with photos
self-host a shared itinerary for family
plan hiking or cycling routes for a trip
how_to_run: ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32) docker run -d --name trek -p 3000:3000 -e ENCRYPTION_KEY=$ENCRYPTION_KEY -e COOKIE_SECURE=false -v ./data:/app/data -v ./uploads:/app/uploads mauriceboe/trek
Open http://<host>:3000 and sign in with the admin credentials (set via ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD, or printed in docker logs trek)
For production: docker compose up -d using the docker-compose.yml shipped in the repository
Helm: helm repo add trek <repo-url>; helm repo update; helm install trek trek/trek
Put TREK behind a TLS reverse proxy that supports WebSocket upgrades on /ws
notable: Optional addons toggled by an admin, including Journey, MCP server, AI assistant, Road trip, Dawarich and AirTrail integrations
Tour planning with routing by hiking SAC grade, ski pistes, paddle water routes and 3D terrain maps
Offline support: installable PWA with per-user IndexedDB store and queued offline writes
Plugin system with sandboxed child processes and a signed plugin registry
Cost splitting in integer cents with multiple payers and settle-up suggestions
caveats: Requires HTTPS behind a reverse proxy for production and WebSocket upgrade support on /ws; the MCP addon also needs Mcp-Session-Id passthrough
COOKIE_SECURE=false is only for plain HTTP testing; login sessions fail without HTTPS otherwise
Several major features (Journey, AI assistant, MCP, Road trip, Collections) are off by default and must be enabled by an admin
Some integrations (Google Places, Amap, AI providers) need your own API keys
